neurons and neurotransmitters in the nervous system. The pro-
duction of neurotransmitters requires adequate amounts of 
nutrients. Among these nutrients are amino acids (tryptophan, 
tyrosine, and glutamine), minerals (zinc, copper, iron, sele-
nium, magnesium), and B vitamins (B1, B2, B3, B6, B12, folic 
acid). These neurotransmitters and nutrients coordinate com-
munication within the body and between the body and the 
environment. People often ask the question “Which nutrients 
are important for proper nervous system functioning, includ-
ing mood?” The proper response is simply, “All of them”.
BOX 41-1  How Nutrients Affect Mental 
Health
Nutrients can affect mental health through a variety of actions:
 1. Nutrients can support or interfere with normal development of the 
brain and central nervous system.
 2. Nutrients may serve as precursors to neurotransmitters.
 3. Macronutrients act as an energy source for the brain.
 4. Nutrients influence genetic transcription.
 5. Nutrients function differently in pharmacologic doses than at nutrio-
logic (food based) doses.
 6. Nutrients contribute to mood, and sense of well-being.
 7. Nutrients may enter or exit from cells related to thoughts, emotions, 
and stress.
Reference: Leyse-Wallace R: Nutrition and mental health, Boca Raton, 
Fla, 2013, Taylor and Francis Inc., CRC Press.
